mainTopic: Identifying kosher birds: relying on one or two signs, the crow and its kinds, the white סנונית, and which birds count as תורין or בני יונה for offerings.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב נחמן's rule. Someone who knows all the forbidden birds may eat a bird with one kosher sign. Someone who does not know them needs two signs and must be able to recognize the crow (עורב). A ברייתא shows that other crow-like birds, the זרזיר and the white סנונית, are also forbidden. So the גמרא explains that one must know the crow and every kind of crow. אמימר rules more leniently: any bird with one sign is kosher as long as it is not a דורס, because the פרס and the עזניה are not found in settled areas. רב יהודה then identifies the kosher 'scratching bird' as the white סנונית, and אמימר and מר זוטרא give opposite versions of which kind of that bird is in dispute: the white-bellied or the yellow-bellied. Finally, רחבה reports in the name of רבי יהודה which birds count as תורין and which as בני יונה for offerings. רב דניאל בר רב קטינא begins a challenge whose quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who may rely on one sign and who needs two
steps.stepSummary: Someone who knows the non-kosher birds may eat a bird with one sign. Someone who doesn't know them needs two signs and must be able to recognize a crow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person knows the non-kosher birds and their names, a bird with one kosher sign is kosher. If he does not know them, a bird with one sign is forbidden, but a bird with two signs is kosher, as long as he can recognize a crow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating רב נחמן's rule about relying on kosher signs in birds. How many signs you need depends on whether you know the forbidden birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרס and the עזניה are forbidden birds that have only one kosher sign. So an expert who knows they aren't in front of him can trust one sign. The crow is a forbidden bird with exactly two signs, so a non-expert with a two-sign bird only has to be sure it isn't a crow.

keyTerms.meaning: Expert; someone who is familiar with something
A sign; here, one of the physical signs that show a bird is kosher
Kosher (literally 'pure')
Not kosher (literally 'impure')
Crow or raven

phrases.english: If he was familiar with them and their names,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the forbidden birds listed in the תורה.

phrases.english: a bird that comes with one sign is kosher;
if he was not familiar with them and their names,
with one sign it is not kosher;
with two signs it is kosher,
provided that he recognizes a crow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן's statement from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expert may rely on one sign. A non-expert needs two signs and must be able to recognize the crow.

steps.title: Is the crow the only bird to worry about? The זרזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'recognize a crow' from a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says 'למינו' adds the זרזיר as another forbidden crow-like bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only the crow and nothing else? But a ברייתא teaches: 'עורב' means the crow, and 'למינו' (after its kind), says רבי אליעזר, adds the זרזיר. The חכמים said to him: But the people of כפר תמרתא in יהודה used to eat them because they have a crop! He answered: They too will have to answer for it in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether recognizing the plain crow is really enough. It quotes a ברייתא showing that there is another forbidden bird in the crow family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the זרזיר is a forbidden 'kind' of crow, then a two-sign bird could be a זרזיר and not the ordinary crow. So knowing only the ordinary crow would not protect a person. The people who ate it relied on its crop (זפק), a kosher sign, but רבי אליעזר holds they were wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more?
After its kind; a word in the פסוק that adds related species
A bird in the crow family (often translated starling)
Crop; a pouch in a bird's throat, one of the kosher signs
They will have to answer for it (be judged) in the future

phrases.english: The crow and nothing more?
But isn't it taught: 'Crow' – this is the crow;
'after its kind' – Rabbi Eliezer says:
to include the zarzir.
They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
But didn't the people of Kefar Temarta in Judea
eat them,
because they have a crop!
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הֵן עֲתִידִין לִיתֵּן אֶת הַדִּין.
phrases.english: They too will be judged in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the condition 'provided he recognizes a crow' from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's condition that recognizing the crow is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows that other crow-like birds such as the זרזיר are also forbidden. A two-sign bird might be one of them, so recognizing only the plain crow is not enough.

steps.title: A second example: the white סנונית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a second reading of 'למינהו' adds the white סנונית, which people in the upper גליל ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'למינהו' comes to add the white סנונית; these are the words of רבי אליעזר. They said to him: But the people of the upper גליל eat it, because its gizzard peels! He answered: They too will have to answer for it in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא, which gives a second forbidden bird included by the word 'למינהו'. This adds weight to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The white סנונית has a gizzard whose lining peels off, which is a kosher sign, yet רבי אליעזר still forbids it as a kind of crow. So there is more than one forbidden crow-like bird that can look kosher by its signs.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation
White סנונית (a type of swallow), counted here as a kind of crow
Gizzard
Peels off; the gizzard lining peels, a kosher sign

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'after its kinds'
is to include the white senunit;
the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא אַנְשֵׁי גָּלִיל הָעֶלְיוֹן אוֹכְלִים אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: But don't the people of the upper Galilee eat it,
because its gizzard peels!
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הֵן עֲתִידִין לִיתֵּן אֶת הַדִּין.
phrases.english: They too will be judged in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 2 with a second example.
steps.kashyaTarget: The same condition, 'provided he recognizes a crow'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second crow-like forbidden bird with a kosher sign makes it clearer that recognizing only the plain crow is not enough.

steps.title: He must know the crow and all its kinds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן meant one must recognize the crow and every kind of crow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he must recognize the crow and every kind of crow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by widening רב נחמן's condition. 'Crow' includes every species in the crow family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself stays the same: a non-expert may eat a bird with two signs. Only the condition grows. He must be able to tell apart the crow and all its relatives, such as the זרזיר and the white סנונית.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a corrected understanding
Every kind of crow

steps.whatToRemember: A non-expert may eat a bird with two kosher signs only if he can recognize the crow and every species of crow.

phrases.english: Rather, the crow and every kind of crow.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the scope of a term
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Recognizing only the ordinary crow is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must recognize all species in the crow family.

steps.title: אמימר: one sign is enough if the bird doesn't claw
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that any bird with one kosher sign is kosher, as long as it is not a clawing bird (דורס).
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The הלכה is that a bird that comes with one sign is kosher, as long as it does not claw its prey.
steps.whatsHappening: A later אמורא, אמימר, gives a practical ruling that is more lenient than רב נחמן's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר does not require the person to be an expert. Any bird with one sign is kosher, with one condition: it must not be a דורס, a bird that claws or grabs its food, which is a sign of a forbidden bird.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה
Claws its food; a bird of prey that grabs and tears, a sign of a non-kosher bird

phrases.english: Ameimar said: The halakha is:
a bird that comes with one sign is kosher,
provided that it does not claw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new practical ruling that differs from רב נחמן's rule in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any bird with one kosher sign is kosher as long as it is not a דורס, even for a non-expert.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about רב נחמן's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר how his ruling fits with רב נחמן, who required expertise to rely on one sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What about the rule of רב נחמן?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר. He points out that רב נחמן allowed a one-sign bird only for an expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said a non-expert may not eat a bird with only one sign, because it might be the פרס or the עזניה. אמימר allows it for everyone, so רב אשי wants to know how אמימר deals with רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: That statement of... (pointing to a known ruling)
What? (here, what about it?)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What about that ruling of Rav Naḥman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling from step 5 using רב נחמן's rule from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's lenient ruling that one sign is enough for anyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן required expertise in the forbidden birds before relying on one sign, which goes against אמימר.

steps.title: אמימר: I don't hold like רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that he 'did not hear' רב נחמן's rule, meaning he does not agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear it, which means: I do not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי politely. He does not follow רב נחמן on this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I did not hear it' is a polite way of saying 'I disagree.' אמימר is not saying he never knew the statement. He is saying he does not accept it as the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear it
That is to say
I do not hold that way

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא שמיע לי' here does not mean אמימר never heard רב נחמן's rule. The גמרא itself explains that it means he does not agree with it.

phrases.english: He said to him: I did not hear it,
that is to say, I do not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, כְּלוֹמַר לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How אמימר deals with רב נחמן's stricter rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמימר simply disagrees with רב נחמן.

steps.title: Why there's no worry: the פרס and עזניה aren't around
steps.stepSummary: אמימר explains that the only one-sign forbidden birds, the פרס and the עזניה, do not live in settled areas, so there is nothing to worry about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What worry is there? Because of the פרס and the עזניה? They are not found in settled areas.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר explains why he disagrees with רב נחמן. The birds that worried רב נחמן are not found where people live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's strictness came from the fear that a one-sign bird might be the פרס or the עזניה. אמימר removes that fear: these birds live far from towns. So a one-sign bird found among people can be trusted, as long as it is not a דורס.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there (to worry about)?
A forbidden bird of prey that has only one kosher sign
Another forbidden bird of prey that has only one kosher sign
Settled, inhabited area

steps.whatToRemember: אמימר rules that a bird with one sign is kosher if it does not claw its food. רב נחמן's worry about the פרס and עזניה does not apply, because they are not found in settled areas.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the concern behind רב נחמן's rule rests on a fact about the world: where these birds live. Once that concern is gone, the stricter requirement falls away.

phrases.english: What is there?
Because of the peres and the ozniyya?
They are not in settled areas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind אמימר's disagreement in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing the factual concern behind the opposing view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A one-sign bird might be the פרס or the עזניה, so expertise is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those birds are not found in settled areas, so any one-sign bird that is not a דורס is kosher.

steps.title: The scratching bird is kosher and is the white swallow
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the עוף המסרט may be used for טהרת מצורע, so it is kosher. He identifies it as the white סנונית that רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: The scratching bird may be used to purify a מצורע. This is the white swallow that רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling by רב יהודה about a particular bird. He says it is kosher and tells us which known bird it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only kosher birds may be used in the purification of a מצורע, so calling this bird 'fit for a מצורע' means it is kosher. By connecting it to the white סנונית, רב יהודה links it to an existing argument between רבי אליעזר and חכמים. That sets up the next steps, which ask what exactly they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'scratching bird,' a bird that scratches with its feet
The purification process for a מצורע, which uses two kosher birds
The white swallow
They disagreed

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
The scratching bird is fit for the purification of a metzora,
phrases.notes: Only kosher birds can be used for this (ויקרא 14:4), so he's really telling us this bird is kosher.

phrases.english: and this is the white senunit (swallow)
about which Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages disagreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: עוֹף הַמְסָרֵט – כָּשֵׁר לְטׇהֳרַת מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about a specific bird. It identifies it as the white סנונית that רבי אליעזר and חכמים disputed in the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עוף המסרט is kosher, and it is the white סנונית that רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue about.

steps.title: אמימר's version: the argument is about the yellow-bellied swallow
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says everyone agrees the white-bellied swallow is permitted. The argument is about the yellow-bellied one, and the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: If its belly is white, everyone agrees it is permitted. They argue when its belly is yellow. רבי אליעזר forbids it and the רבנן permit it, and the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר explains that there are two kinds of white swallow, and he tells us which one רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the bird into two types by belly color. The white-bellied one is permitted by everyone. The yellow-bellied one is in dispute, and in practice it is forbidden because the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: White
Yellow
Its belly
Everyone agrees (literally, 'the whole world does not disagree')
The practical הלכה follows this opinion

phrases.english: Ameimar said: With regard to one whose belly is white,
everyone agrees that it is permitted;
where they disagree is with regard to one whose belly is yellow:
Rabbi Eliezer forbids it and the Rabbis permit it,
and the halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains exactly which type of the white סנונית from step 9 is in dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: White-bellied: permitted by all. Yellow-bellied: in dispute, and forbidden in practice (הלכה like רבי אליעזר).

steps.title: מר זוטרא's version: the argument is about the white-bellied swallow
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא reports the opposite version of אמימר: everyone forbids the yellow-bellied swallow, the argument is about the white-bellied one, and the הלכה follows the רבנן, who permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא teaches it this way: If its belly is yellow, everyone agrees it is forbidden. They argue when its belly is white. רבי אליעזר forbids it and the רבנן permit it, and the הלכה follows the רבנן, who permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposite version of אמימר's teaching as reported by מר זוטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version everything flips. The yellow-bellied bird is forbidden by everyone, and the white-bellied bird is the one in dispute. Since the הלכה follows the רבנן, the white-bellied bird is permitted in practice. So the practical result is the same in both versions: the white one is permitted and the yellow one is forbidden. Only the location of the argument changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (a different version of the same teaching)
Forbids / permit

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two versions lead to different practical results. In both, the white-bellied swallow ends up permitted and the yellow-bellied one ends up forbidden. They only disagree about which bird רבי אליעזר and the רבנן were arguing over.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra teaches it like this:
phrases.notes: He is giving his own version of אמימר's statement from the step before.

phrases.english: With regard to one whose belly is yellow,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden.
Where they disagree is with regard to one whose belly is white:
Rabbi Eliezer forbids it and the Rabbis permit it,
and the halacha follows the Rabbis, who permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version of אמימר's statement in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Yellow-bellied: forbidden by all. White-bellied: in dispute, and permitted in practice (הלכה like the רבנן).

steps.title: How can a yellow-bellied bird be called the white swallow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב יהודה's phrase 'white סנונית' fits the version where the argument is about the white-bellied bird. It asks what 'white' could mean in the version where the argument is about the yellow-bellied bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says they argue about the white-bellied bird: that is why רב יהודה said 'this is the white swallow.' But for the one who says they argue about the yellow-bellied bird, what does 'this is the white swallow' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר's version from step 10 by checking it against רב יהודה's wording in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה called the disputed bird 'the white סנונית.' That fits מר זוטרא's version, where the disputed bird has a white belly. In אמימר's version, though, the disputed bird has a yellow belly, so the word 'white' seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (according to one view), used to set up a contrast with another view
According to the one who says
What (is meant by)?

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says
that they disagree about the one whose belly is white;
that is why he teaches: 'This is the white senunit.'
But according to the one who says they disagree about the yellow one,
what is meant by 'This is the white senunit'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּחִיוָּרָא כְּרֵסַהּ פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two versions in steps 10-11 against רב יהודה's words in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's version (step 10), which places the argument on the yellow-bellied bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה called the disputed bird 'white.' If the disputed bird has a yellow belly, why call it white?

steps.title: 'White' only rules out the black house swallow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'white' is not about the belly. It tells this bird apart from the black swallow that lives in houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the house swallow, which is black.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אמימר's version by explaining the word 'white' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'White swallow' is the name of the whole species, as opposed to the black house swallow. So even the yellow-bellied type belongs to the 'white' species. That way רב יהודה's wording fits אמימר's version too, and both versions still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
Of the houses (the kind that lives in houses)
Black

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree in practice: the white-bellied swallow is permitted and the yellow-bellied one is forbidden. 'White swallow' is the name of the species, as opposed to the black house swallow.

phrases.english: To exclude the house one, which is black.
phrases.notes: In other words, 'white' names the whole kind of bird, not the color of its belly.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the word 'white' as a contrast with another species, not a description of the belly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'White' describes the belly, so the disputed bird must be the white-bellied one.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'White' only distinguishes this species from the black house swallow, so אמימר's version also fits רב יהודה's words.

steps.title: Sorting birds into turtledoves and young pigeons
steps.stepSummary: רחבה quotes רבי יהודה: the תסיל is a kind of בני יונה. The דאציפי and the תורין של רחבה are kinds of תורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה said in the name of רבי יהודה: A תסיל is unfit to be brought as a turtledove, but it is fit to be brought as a young pigeon. The דאציפי and the turtledoves of רחבה are fit to be brought as turtledoves, but they are unfit to be brought as young pigeons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רבי יהודה, reported by רחבה, that tells us which family certain birds belong to for bird offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only two kinds of birds can be brought as a קרבן: תורין, which are fit only when grown, and בני יונה, which are fit only when young. By saying a תסיל works as בני יונה but not as תורין, רבי יהודה puts it in the pigeon family. The דאציפי and the תורין של רחבה work the opposite way, so they are in the turtledove family.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves, one of the two kinds of birds fit for a קרבן. They are fit only when grown.
Young pigeons, the other kind of bird fit for a קרבן. They are fit only when young.
A bird that looks like a dove. Here it is classed as a kind of pigeon.
A kind of bird that is classed here as a turtledove.
Fit / unfit to be brought as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two families up. A bird that is 'fit as בני יונה' is in the pigeon family, so it can be brought only while young. A bird that is 'fit as תורין' is in the turtledove family, so it can be brought only when grown.
steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the גמרא's work of identifying birds by name. It shows that one bird can be fit under one name and unfit under the other.

phrases.english: Rachava said that Rabbi Yehuda said:
A tasil is unfit as a turtledove,
phrases.notes: He means a young תסיל. That is why it fails as a turtledove, since turtledoves are brought only when grown.

phrases.english: but it is fit as a young pigeon.
Datzifi birds and the turtledoves of Reḥava
phrases.notes: רחבה here is the name of a place, not the רחבה who is reporting the ruling.

phrases.english: are fit as turtledoves,
but unfit as young pigeons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of the עוף המסרט and the white סנונית, the גמרא brings a new ruling, reported by רחבה in the name of רבי יהודה, that identifies birds for the purpose of bird offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תסיל is in the בני יונה family. The דאציפי and the תורין של רחבה are in the תורין family.
